artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

artifacts.title: Morton Smith v. Western Carolina
artifacts.synopsis: Complaint of TE Morton H. Smith vs. Western Carolina Presbytery. The SJC sustained Smith's complaint in part, finding that Presbytery erred procedurally by immediately adopting a judgment against RE Payne's views without process. The SJC annulled the declaration made by Presbytery regarding RE Payne's views and remanded the case for proper adjudication.

matches.evidence: Declining to address case-specific questions, the CCB outlined the three BCO provisions by which members may be removed from church rolls: transfer, discipline, or relocation.

artifacts.title: Procedure for removing members who relocate without affiliating elsewhere

matches.evidence: BCO 46-2 governs removal of members who move away and fail to affiliate within a year; BCO 46-5's formal discipline applies only to willful neglect, not mere relocation.
